A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same black-box watermarking work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original watermark detection, distortion, generation-quality, and attack experiments, including the results in Tables 1–7 and appendix simulations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds an empirical diagnostic concerning the seed-independence assumption in Appendix A.2, Figure 8, and Table 8.

M1.justification: The proposed flat and recursive watermarking procedures, candidate-selection rule, and detection algorithms remain unchanged in Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix B. The corrected baseline formulas do not introduce a new watermarking component.

E1.justification: Both versions use databricks-dolly-15k and eli5-category, with C4-realnewslike for baseline calibration. The new diagnostic samples existing Dolly coverage; it adds no dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, but Section 5.4 corrects the reported Aaronson Corrected scoring rule from complementary CDFs to CDFs, including its Irwin–Hall alternative. This is a revision to the documented baseline rule; unchanged comparison results do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E3.justification: The added diagnostic uses 20 random Dolly prompts, 250–300-token outputs, m=32, n=1–4 with k=1, and an additional n=4, k=10 condition. These introduce a limited new evaluation design; the existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a targeted diagnostic of the independence assumption by examining candidate-score uniformity across n and k settings. Figure 8 and Table 8 supplement the retained distribution, detection, and attack analyses.

E5.justification: v3 introduces a two-sided Kolmogorov–Smirnov test with reported statistics and p-values for the new diagnostic. The existing repeated-generation standard-error reporting is retained, without an explicit increase in its run counts.

E6.justification: Figure 8 and Table 8 add empirical-CDF and KS results. For k=1 and m=32, the KS statistic increases from 0.0122 at n=4 to 0.0920 at n=1. Numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the plotted content of Figures 1–7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.4 corrects the mathematical definitions of the Aaronson Corrected scores by removing the leading 1-minus terms, aligning their direction with higher scores indicating watermarking. Theorems 4.1–4.4, their assumptions, and the substantive appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about black-box access, distortion-free watermarking under assumptions, recursive composition, performance guarantees, and competitiveness with white-box schemes.

C2.justification: The new appendix discussion links smaller n to seed reuse and distortion, explaining a tradeoff with attack robustness. A new Broader Impacts section discusses provenance benefits and the privacy risk of providers tracking published outputs without users knowing.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 documents how candidate u_i values are tracked and pooled across decoding steps and prompts for the new diagnostic. Existing implementation code, Gemini prompts, and model/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive novelty distinctions are retained. The SynthID and WaterMax comparisons move from Related Work to a 'Relation to similar work' passage after the algorithm description, preserving their technical positioning.

P1.justification: v3 relocates the two closest-method comparisons, adds the Broader Impacts and diagnostic passages, and makes localized wording and notation edits. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide retypesetting changes fonts, text width, publication headers, and display sizing and placement. Figure 1 moves from page 9 to page 11, appendix figures are regrouped, and Figure 8 and Table 8 are added. Existing plot content and table organization are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the detection-score polarity inconsistency in Section 5.4 and adds useful evidence about practical departures from uniformity, plus concrete privacy considerations. These are limited improvements to correctness and interpretation. The new KS diagnostic does not by itself establish seed independence, so it only partly addresses the theoretical assumption's empirical justification; the main results and guarantees are unchanged.
